doc.title: Jerry Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe and Christian Goodwillie, via Zoom, June 30, 2021

title: Desert island discs and the Sam Goody mono sale
summary: Asked about desert island discs, Gordon tells of the Sam Goody mono sale and the hippie salesman who steered him to jazz.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Well I’ve got to say as a preface to my last question I want to thank Monk for allowing me to be a special guest in one of his interviews ‘cause he’s a true pro, and he might hate me for asking this question but any Desert Island discs, Jerry? From either ones you put out or just in your life?
I love that question because I have over a hundred desert island discs. But I like to talk about that all the time on my radio show.

I like to talk about it and say, announce, “Okay here’s one of my desert island discs.” The first two jazz albums I bought — I would like to tell this story. I used to shop at Sam Goody’s in Center City, Philadelphia. And every week they would take out a column, kind of a big column, I’d say a third of a page top to bottom with a weekly ad in the Philadelphia Inquirer, the number one newspaper. And they would have different labels on sale every week. Okay? Oh my God all Warner Brothers is on sale, you know, and it would be cheap. And this is in my younger days now, teenager, and I was still buying mono records. And with the Sam Goody ad you could buy, Christian, like the new Grateful Dead album, the first, for $1.99 in mono. You know. I mean that’s where it was at. We didn’t even have a stereo at my house. So one day, and I did this every Saturday. One day I’m looking at the ad in the Inquirer, “Mono Records — we’re clearing out all our mono records. One dollar.” Oh my God okay, like I flew down there, dollar records. There was a salesman, I’m sorry I’m so verbose on this, on all my answers, but there is a salesman at Sam Goody’s he was a hippie. He was the only hippie I knew. He was the first hippie I ever had any contact with and spoke to or spoke to me. And he wore this weird suit, the same one every week, every Saturday, had big lapels. He would have this like wild flower tie, you know, and we would talk music. “Hey how’s the new Frank Zappa album?” You know? “How’s the new, you know, Grateful Dead album?” So he was my inside guy to music. So I get there for the mono sale, I say, “Oh my God where is everything? Where’s the stuff? What should I get?” He said, “Gee Jerry, you’re really kind of late, I mean people came in like locusts and cleaned us out of all the rock records for a dollar, are you kidding?” We got cleaned out. I guess the sale had gone on for a week, or whatever it was, a couple of days. So I say oh I can’t believe it. He said, “Are you into jazz?” I said, “Jazz, I don’t listen to jazz, what’s jazz?” And he said, “No, man, jazz is really cool.” That is verbatim. And I said, “What? All right, I’ll listen to you.” So we walk over to the jazz section and he hands me two albums in mono, a dollar each. Guess what one of them was? What is the number one desert island disc for anyone regardless of their age, in jazz? Monk knows. Christian you should know too.
